_doc: virtualization-audit.json — handover v2 artifact for Priority 3 (verified reversible virtualization-off A/B). Read-only audit result; NO boot parameter was changed by this audit. Sources: docs/benchmarks/iommu-decision-20260915.md, boot-arms-result-D-blocked-C-breaks-gpu-20260915.md.
question: Can we measure a decode/prefill gain from turning off virtualization / IOMMU, reversibly, on this box?
answer: NO — the lever is closed on this machine. Blocked by security posture on the intended arm and destructive to HIP device access on the other. This is a real negative result, not an untested option.

runtime_state_baseline.RequiredSecurityProperties_meaning: base virtualization is REQUIRED — VBS cannot run without the hypervisor
runtime_state_baseline.host_iommu_device: none exposed (Get-PnpDevice for IOMMU|SMMU|DMA Remap returns nothing; only HVCI/bit2 running)

A_baseline.note: the machine's normal state; every number in measured-baseline.json was taken here

D_no_hypervisor.why_override: EnableVirtualizationBasedSecurity=1 + RequiredSecurityProperties include base virtualization; VBS cannot run without the hypervisor so the boot flag is overridden. WSL2 still worked on this boot, independently confirming the hypervisor ran.

C_no_vsm_no_hv_iommu_policy.symptom: ROCm/HIP cannot query the GPU: stdout device enumeration empty (0 bytes), cudaMemGetInfo failed (invalid argument) at 0.30s, never reaches threadpool init or listening
C_no_vsm_no_hv_iommu_policy.caveat: did not isolate which of the two settings (vsmlaunchtype vs hypervisoriommupolicy) breaks it; practical answer is the same either way
C_no_vsm_no_hv_iommu_policy.reversible: yes — boot-entry setting, not damage; rebooting the normal entry restores the GPU

B_vsm_off_hypervisor_on.reason_not_run: shares vsmlaunchtype Off with the arm-C breakage and VBS ignored the same flag on arm D; expected to break the GPU or be overridden — not worth a reboot each way

why_transfer_is_impossible_here.source_finding: r/StrixHalo/1wdrkrc (baldlawyer): amd_iommu=off raised prefill +1.8%..+31.6% depending on model on bare-metal Linux; decode unaffected (+-1%); not a power/clock effect
why_transfer_is_impossible_here.our_fast_path_is_not_bare_metal_linux: native Windows HIP (clang 24 / TheRock) — amd_iommu=off does not exist; Windows uses Device Guard/Kernel DMA Protection
why_transfer_is_impossible_here.wsl_path_is_paravirtual: WSL2 boots paravirtualized on Hyper-V with a VIRTUAL IOMMU (Default domain type: Translated), not AMD-Vi; no /sys/class/iommu; .wslconfig sets no kernelCommandLine
why_transfer_is_impossible_here.conclusion: a WSL amd_iommu=off test would toggle a virtual guest IOMMU and prove nothing about the host effect

consequences_if_it_did_apply_bare_metal: disables the NPU (same parameter removes the NPU device path) — founder wants the NPU used
turns off DMA translation machine-wide (security/isolation change)
even then: source's ROCm/MoE rows were only +1.8%..+6.0%, i.e. ~+19..+63 t/s on our 1057 t/s prefill — still short of ilintar 1204, at the cost of the NPU

gate_status.actions_taken_by_this_audit: NONE — read-only; no boot parameter changed, no reboot performed
gate_status.recommendation: DO NOT change boot parameters. Keep the machine's security posture intact. The prefill gap is better attacked with real RDNA3.5 kernel work (source-manifest.md S9/S10), not via a bare-metal-only boot flag we cannot reach.

test_boot_entries: {f26c7219-...} Strix bench - no VSM + no hv IOMMU policy
cleanup_todo.note: windows-boot-ab.ps1 -Restore armed the normal entry; -RemoveAll should be run to delete the two test entries. Deleting a BCD entry is a maintenance action — confirm owner approval before running.
